{
  "paraphrased_article": "She is the psychic daughter of one of Europe's longest-reigning kings; he is a self-proclaimed sixth-generation shaman hailing from California. The marriage of Princess Märtha Louise of Norway to Durek Verrett on Saturday afternoon was far from a typical royal event, yet that didn't deter onlookers from gathering along the cloudy streets of Geiranger to try to catch a view of the bride.

The sole daughter of King Harald and Queen Sonja, the 52-year-old princess is fourth in the line of succession to Norway's throne. She wed the 49-year-old Verrett in a traditional Church of Norway ceremony, held at the four-star Hotel Union in a quaint village nestled beneath the Geiranger fjord, with royals and celebrities in attendance.

The princess was accompanied by seven bridesmaids, among them her teenage daughters Leah and Emma Behn from her previous marriage to the late Norwegian writer Ari Behn, from whom she separated in 2017.

The 350-person guest list featured Märtha Louise's brother, Crown Prince Haakon, along with his wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit; Sweden's Crown Princess Victoria and her husband, Prince Daniel; as well as Prince Constantijn and Princess Laurentien of the Netherlands.

Princess Märtha Louise has led a life far removed from royal convention, having previously proclaimed herself a psychic and spent around ten years operating a healing school where she instructed people on how to communicate with angels. In 2022, she announced she would relinquish her official royal responsibilities in order to concentrate on the business ventures she shares with Verrett and to create a clearer separation between their personal endeavors and the Norwegian royal house.

Verrett presents himself on Instagram as a 'servant of God' and an 'energy activator.' Among his high-profile clients is Gwyneth Paltrow, the founder of Goop, whom he has referred to as a 'soul sister.'"
}
```
